docs.description: FMPSG022 -titan- Starts off with 3 tracks weighing in at over 20 minutes-- titanic!  Thankfully, this one stays more than afloat. They should have built the actual Titanic ship with copies of volumes from the FMPSG series because this shit never sinks.   Track 3, an original, deserves special highlight in that bunch. If a 7 minute long Ys track has you on edge, you put on track 3, put the top down on your convertible and cruise. Maybe in Vice City with a custom soundtrack, that's how I have to do it too. The driving beat somehow brings to mind the smooth grooves of Neu and also the clickety-clacky garage beats of another Krautrock group, Can. and I'd say this sounds like Kraftwerk but that could be said of 99% of chiptune tracks, so why bother! Anyway, this volume is almost a straight split of original tracks and shmup game tracks. But there is, as has been the case since a few volumes ago, an anime section (Kantai Collection and Sword Art Online II, both scorching of course.) And a great live action Japanese TV show track, which also is getting heavily repped lately too - Tokusou Saizensen track 12. Even has some "chip vocaloid" for lack of a better term.

docs.description: If you haven’t played a video game since the Tetris days — or ever — you’d be very surprised how engrossing and how captivating they are now. The medium is unique in its ability to make people feel like we’re part of a story, rather than just watching it. Video games shape identity in a way that’s distinct from other pop culture. We talk about games from Metroid, Quake, and Tomb Raider to Call of Duty and Pokemon. This episode features Sam Riedel, Saud Al-Zaid, and music from artist Sammus. Source: https://soundcloud.com/bitch-media/video-games-and-identity Uploader: Bitch Media

docs.description: This is a complete overhaul of an older series of videos about horror movies that have never legally made it to DVD, Blu-Ray, or Digital. Several titles were removed but even more were added. Due to the nature of this episode a lot of the available images are very low quality, non existent, or had to be converted from my personal copies. I apologize for the quality, I used the best sources available. Minor correction: when talking about the last film I reference the website 3blackchicks.com and their review. My phrasing makes it sound like the website itself was abandoned but it is really only this particular part of it that seems abandoned. Sorry for any confusion. No revenue is generated from this video. Now that this project has completed, it's so cool to be able to look back on it! While working on this series of videos, it felt like the most strenuous project I ever took upon myself. Looking back, it really wasn't that bad! I suppose that's how most things in life go. I'm looking forward to getting back to creating my normal videos! It's been quite a while since I recorded one, and I'm definitely feeling the itch to get creating again! If you're an ensemble looking to perform this arrangement somewhere, you have my permission to do so! I would love to see a video recording as well. You must be pretty fortunate and/or crazy to attempt playing this, kudos to you! docs.description: On this episode of the show, we’ll be talking about the Middle Ages: that period in European history that most of us learned about through Game of Thrones and Robin Hood. We think of it as racially homogenous, rigidly gendered, and brutish, but scholars like the ones Soleil talks to in today’s show have more nuanced interpretations. And yet, white supremacists within the alt right are attempting to claim the Middle Ages for their own political ends. What is the truth, and why does it matter? First, you’ll hear from Dr. Tory Pearman on the lives and public perception of people with disabilities in Medieval Europe. Then, Dr. Dorothy Kim elaborates on the connections between the alt right and Medieval Studies and what scholars like her are doing to take back control over the field they love. Source: https://soundcloud.com/bitch-media/popaganda-the-fight-for-the-middle-ages Uploader: Bitch Media

docs.description: As the right dominates many online spaces, Briahna asks two prominent creators how more progressive voices can reach audiences on platforms like YouTube and Twitch. Jim Sterling is an independent video game journalist and commentator whose YouTube channel skewers the “AAA” gaming industry for its exploitation of both workers and customers. Hasan Piker, a journalist with The Young Turks, also livestreams on Twitch as HasanAbi, where he pushes back against right-wing arguments while chatting with thousands of followers. docs.description: Facebook's built a food app most of us can't use, and shouting at Google Docs now will get you somewhere. I'm Amy Guth and this is The Feed on Rivet. Facebook's been upfront about wanting to rule video, and to prove it, it's made deals with many music artists including Carrie Underwood, Alicia Keys, and now, U2, to debut exclusive music videos on the site. While Facebook probably wouldn't thumb it's nose at any video, the realm of music videos is especially enticing: indeed, music videos make up nearly 40% of content on competitor Google-owned YouTube. A Florida school board has announced a new system to monitor the social media accounts of its students, an effort they say will curb cyber-bullying and serve as an early-warning system for threats of violence. Students and parents say the move is a privacy violation, but the school board maintains that it's only viewing information already in the public sphere, so it's fair game for monitoring. Facebook's built an impressive food-ordering app on its React Native framework-- but it's only for Facebook employees. In a blog post, Facebook described how the app allows its workers to order food from one of the internal employee restaurants, pick it up within 15 minutes, and how the system will continually fine-tune and customize the menu much in the way it curates our newsfeeds. A Google Docs update now allows users to write with voice commands. By enabling this feature, users can create document text just by talking, which works reasonably well for simple sentences, if you're in a room with low background noise, and can still access your keyboard to tweak words as you go. Or, hey, roll with it and see what happens: Game he tooth, texting stew feather of Google ducks on ribbon. That's The Feed on Rivet. I'm Amy Guth.

docs.description: Similar to my thirty-fifth anniversary Final Fantasy music collection, this thirtieth anniversary collection contains every official song made for the Legend of Zelda series from 1986 to 2016, as well as the soundtrack of the Ben Drowned story by Jadusable. The reason it's only the first thirty years is because I excluded anything after the Switch's release in 2017, meaning no BotW or TotK, for example, because, to be honest, Nintendo is scary. This was much less of a pain to compile in comparison to Final Fantasy, as there is a lot less content overall, and nowhere near as many side games or arrangement albums. If anything is missing, it's because it released during or after 2017, as explained above. I hope you enjoy the collection.

docs.description: The TRIFORCE of BASS is a collection of 3 EPs spanning a variety of games from The Legend of Zelda series. As varied as the games are, so are the producers on this EP. Mykah is a DJ from Liverpool UK, bringing a tribal, moombah and drum'n'bass influences. dj-Jo is a FL Studio producer from Florida who wilds the heaviest synths and intense drum production. Dj CUTMAN and Spamtron remix and remaster their classic EP Bagu and the Riverman with DJ friendly edits with a new level of clarity in the mix. The TRIFORCE of BASS spans multiple generations of Zelda music, from the original Overworld theme, to The Palace theme from Zelda II and the Dungeon from A Link to the Past. Other tracks are inspired by Link's Awakening, Wind Waker, and Skyward Sword.

docs.description: Activism Panel at Vida Vegan Con Sunday 28 August 2011, Portland Oregon, USA Panelists: Leigh-Chantelle of Viva la Vegan!
